details: On June 2, 2026, the U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on Nobitex, Iran's largest digital asset exchange, and three other platforms (Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex) as part of its "Economic Wrath" campaign. The Treasury accused these exchanges of facilitating Iran's efforts to circumvent international sanctions, transfer capital abroad, and support entities like the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Nobitex reportedly processed over 50% of Iran's digital asset inflows in 2025. This move aims to disrupt Tehran's use of digital assets to sustain its economy amidst an economic crisis.
title: US Sanctions Nobitex and Three Other Iranian Cryptocurrency Exchanges

details: Bitcoin experienced a significant price drop on June 3, 2026, briefly falling below $66,000 and reaching its lowest level since April. This downturn is largely attributed to escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly concerns around the Strait of Hormuz, which are driving fears of rising energy prices and inflationary pressures. Simultaneously, the cryptocurrency market is facing sustained pressure from record outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs), with approximately $742 million in liquidations triggered and the total crypto market capitalization dropping by $140 billion in one day.
title: Bitcoin Dips to $66K as Middle East Tensions & ETF Outflows Persist

details: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz since late February 2026, causing severe disruptions to global energy supplies. The Strait, a vital passage for approximately 20% of the world's crude oil, has seen WTI Crude Oil futures surge above $112 per barrel. This has resulted in a significant increase in transportation fuel costs, with U.S. retail average gas prices surpassing $4.63 per gallon in May. The elevated energy prices are contributing to global inflationary pressures and complicating the monetary policy decisions of central banks.
title: Strait of Hormuz Closure Fuels Energy Price Surge and Inflation
